Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; John Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; and David Patel, VP of Exploration.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Reynolds.

Mike Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved robust performance in our refining segment with high throughput, solid margins, and top-tier efficiency. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on production growth and guidance for the coming periods. We posted impressive proved reserves additions, achieving a reserve replacement ratio well above targets through organic means. Further, we demonstrated capital discipline with our capex breakdown coming in under budget across drilling, completions, and facilities. Finally, we are taking steps to optimize capital allocation, prioritizing dividends, share buybacks, and high-return reinvestments.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Harlan to discuss our financial results in more detail.

John Harlan: Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $5.2 billion, up 12% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.1 billion, and net income was $850 million. We generated $1.2 billion in free cash flow and returned $600 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $8 billion in debt and $3.5 billion in cash.

Good morning, everyone. Moving to our production guidance for Q4 and full-year 2025, we're pleased to reaffirm our disciplined, returns-focused approach to capital deployment, which continues to drive peer-leading capital efficiency and free cash flow generation.

For the fourth quarter of 2024, we expect average daily production of 425,000 to 450,000 BOE per day, representing roughly a 3% to 8% sequential increase from our Q3 actuals of 412,000 BOE/d. Oil volumes should comprise about 62% of the total, or 265,000 to 280,000 barrels per day, with NGLs at 15% and natural gas making up the balance. This guidance embeds approximately 25,000 BOE/d of new production from our ongoing drilling and completions program, offset modestly by planned downtime.

Looking further out, our full-year 2025 production guidance is 460,000 to 485,000 BOE/d, a solid 12% to 18% growth at the midpoint over 2024's estimated 410,000 BOE/d. This translates to oil volumes of 285,000 to 300,000 barrels per day at a 62% mix, supported by a $1.6 billion D&C capital program—flat to last year but allocated more efficiently across our high-return inventory. At the midpoint, this implies about 110,000 BOE/d of net adds for the year, with quarterly builds ramping from Q1's estimated 445,000 BOE/d to Q4's 475,000 to 500,000 BOE/d range.

Now, let's unpack the key factors influencing these projections, starting with the positives. Our Permian Basin core—which accounts for 70% of our 2025 oil production—remains the engine of growth. We've turned to the plate with 45 gross operated wells brought online in Q3, posting average 30-day IP rates of 1,800 barrels of oil per day and 12 MMcf/d of gas, thanks to our optimized 12,500-foot laterals in the Midland Basin's Northern shelf and 2nd Bone Spring plays. EURs here are tracking at 1.4 MMBOE per well, up 15% YoY from enhanced proppant loading—now at 2,500 lbs/ft—and diverter tech that's improved cluster efficiency to over 85%. We're pacing 220 gross operated wells in 2025, with D&C costs down to $850 per lateral foot, firmly in the lowest quartile per Enverus analytics.

Regionally, the Eagle Ford—20% of portfolio—will contribute 45,000 BOE/d in 2025, flat YoY but with 10% higher oil cut from our Pearsall extension pilots. Early results from four-window fracs are exceeding type curve by 20% on IP, driven by our partnership with Halliburton on dissolvable ball tech to accelerate flowback. In the DJ Basin—8% mix—we're layering in 15,000 BOE/d from Niobrara C-sand horizontals, where we've reduced cycle times to 45 days spud-to-sales via centralized pad drilling—mirroring efficiencies seen at peers like Occidental and EOG.

On the technical front, our digital initiatives are yielding tangible uplift. We've rolled out AI-driven seismic inversion across 80% of our Permian acreage, identifying 15 upside locations previously derisked from 10 MMBOE to 1.2 MMBOE EURs. Real-time frac monitoring with fiber optics has cut screen-outs by 40%, and our proprietary cube development model—stacking 48-well pads in the Delaware—boosts capital efficiency by 25% versus standalone drilling. ESG-wise, electrified frack fleets now cover 60% of activity, shaving methane intensity to 0.15% and positioning us ahead of SEC disclosure curves.

Strategically, this guidance assumes WTI in the $70 to $80 per barrel range—our half-cycle breakeven remains $45 WTI equivalent—and modest Henry Hub gas at $2.75 to $3.25. We've hedged 55% of 2025 oil volumes at $74.50 floor via collars and swaps, protecting FCF even in a $60 trough. Inventory-wise, we see 7 years of Tier 1 locations—IRRs >60% at $60 WTI—giving us optionality to high-grade toward longer laterals and parent-child sequencing.

Of course, no outlook is without risks. Q4 embeds 10,000 BOE/d of turnaround downtime at our Pecos processing plant, now resolved post-Q3. Broader headwinds include OPEC+ quota adherence, which we've factored at 95% compliance extending into H1 2025, supporting realizations; but prolonged underperformance could pressure service costs. Supply chain for Tier 1 sand remains tight—up 8% QoQ—but our forward contracts with Hi-Crush mitigate this. Regulatory scrutiny in the Permian, including BLM venting rules and potential Delaware Basin curtailments, caps our gas capture at 92% for now. Weather risk is low post-hurricane season, but we've stress-tested for a 5% volume haircut in Gulf-adjacent ops.

Internationally, our 10% stake in the ExxonMobil-led Stabroek block offshore Guyana adds long-dated upside—Yellowtail FPSO onlineing Q4 supports 2,000 BOE/d net to us in 2025—but we're guiding conservatively pending FID on Uaru. No material M&A baked in, though our $2.5 billion liquidity gives bolt-on flexibility akin to recent Concho-Delek deals.

In summary, this guidance reflects a balanced portfolio delivering 15%+ compounded growth through decade-end, with 70%+ FCF yield at strip prices. We're prioritizing returns over barrels.

Before moving on, I'd like to touch on our proved reserves additions for the year to date, building toward a strong year-end position. Maintaining a robust reserve replacement ratio—or RRR—is the lifeblood of any upstream operator like Apex. It ensures long-term sustainability, supports our free cash flow generation, and underpins our multi-year dividend growth trajectory. We're on track for total proved reserves to reach around 2.8 billion barrels of oil equivalent at year-end—up approximately 18% from the start of the year.

Our total proved reserves additions YTD stand at about 285 million BOE, comprising positive revisions, extensions and discoveries, and a modest acquisition component. To put this in context, our 2024 production is tracking toward 152 million BOE—a 5% increase year-over-year, driven by our high-margin shale assets and ramping deepwater Gulf production. This positions us for a total RRR of 188%—well above our long-term target of 120% and in line with top-tier peers like Pioneer Natural Resources or ConocoPhillips. Excluding acquisitions, our organic RRR—which we view as the purest measure of our exploration and development engine—clocked in at 165%. That's organic growth at its finest.

Breaking down the components: Extensions and discoveries contributed 185 million BOE, or 65% of total additions, fueled by our aggressive drilling across 1,200 gross operated wells. In the Permian Basin, our Delaware sub-basin stack plays delivered 95 million BOE through 45 successful Wolfcamp and Bone Spring extensions. We've optimized lateral lengths to 12,000 feet with our proprietary ApexStim hydraulic fracturing design—a high-intensity slickwater frac with 4,500 pounds of proppant per foot—achieving initial production rates 25% above basin type curves. Recycle ratios here improved to $8.50/BOE from $9.20 last year, thanks to lower F&D costs of $12/BOE.

Positive revisions added 72 million BOE, primarily from performance upsides in our Eagle Ford and Gulf of Mexico assets. In the Eagle Ford, better-than-expected EURs from our prior infill campaign added 35 million BOE; we're now booking P1 locations at 800,000 BOE per 10,000-foot lateral, up 15% YoY. Gulf of Mexico deepwater revisions stemmed from our King's Quay FPSO ramp-up, where we've sanctioned Phase 2 development adding 25 million BOE at sub-$40/BOE breakevens—competitive with ExxonMobil's Guyana assets.

Acquisitions included a tuck-in deal for 28 million BOE in the DJ Basin, acquired for $350 million net—at a sub-$12/BOE cost, accretive to our NAV and instantly NAV-positive at current WTI strip prices around $75/bbl.

Regionally, the U.S. onshore shale portfolio—70% of our additions—continues to dominate, with the Permian contributing 55% of organic growth. This reflects our 3D seismic reprocessing and machine learning reservoir modeling, which unlocked 20% more Tier 1 inventory than prior assessments. Internationally, our North Sea assets added 12 million BOE via a Judy/Joanne appraisal sidetrack, while our Brazil pre-salt block—partnered with Petrobras—booked first proved reserves of 18 million BOE from the recent Buzios extension well—positioning us for FPSO tie-backs by 2026.

Strategically, this isn't just about replacing reserves; it's about organic growth fueling embedded value. Our drilling inventory now stands at 7+ years of Tier 1 locations at $50/bbl WTI, with half-day cycle times in the Permian averaging 18 days. We've layered in ESG initiatives like our CCUS pilots in the Permian, qualifying 15 million BOE for enhanced oil recovery tax credits under Section 45Q, which bolsters proved developed producing bookings. Year-over-year, organic RRR improved despite a softer commodity backdrop mid-year, underscoring the quality of our portfolio amid OPEC+ cuts and LNG demand tailwinds.

Looking forward, we see sustained RRR above 150% through the decade, supported by our capex plan—prioritizing capital efficiency, with Permian half-cycle returns north of 80%.

Shifting to our capital expenditure breakdown for drilling, completions, and facilities—budget versus actual. This quarter, we continue to demonstrate disciplined capital allocation amid a volatile macro environment, with WTI averaging around $82 per barrel and natural gas lingering in the $2.50 to $3.00 Mcf range. Our total upstream capex guidance for 2024 remains at $1.15 to $1.25 billion, and we're tracking right in the middle of that at actual spend of $1.12 billion year-to-date, or about 2% under our internal budget.

Drilling capex: budget $620 million versus actual $595 million—a 4% underrun. Drilling represented 53% of our total capex budget this year, reflecting our emphasis on high-return inventory development. Year-to-date, we've spudded 42 wells against a budget of 45, primarily due to proactive rig scheduling optimizations. This was driven by operational efficiencies in the Permian, where our two contracted Walker Ridge SuperSpec rigs achieved average drilling times of 18 days per 12,000-foot lateral, a 15% improvement over last year. This was enabled by advanced rotary steerable systems and real-time geosteering with LWD tools, reducing doglegs and non-productive time to under 5%.

Permian drilling absorbed 65% of this bucket at $385 million actual versus $400 million budget, benefiting from lower day rates as the U.S. rig count dipped. In the Eagle Ford, we deferred two exploratory spuds amid softer condensate realizations, saving $8 million. Bakken drilling came in on budget. Drilling costs per lateral foot fell 8% YoY to $450 per foot, outpacing industry averages.

Completions capex: budget $380 million versus actual $405 million—a 7% overrun. Completions, at 33% of budget, saw front-loading to capture Q4 IP rates. We've completed and brought online 38 wells YTD versus 35 budgeted, focusing on engineered frac designs. The overrun stemmed from inflationary pressures on proppant and sand—up 12% QoQ—and higher zipper frac efficiencies on our 7-well pads in the Permian. There, dissolvable diverter tech boosted stage counts by 20% to 55 stages per well, enhancing EURs by 10% to 1.2 Mboe per 1,000-foot lateral. Eagle Ford aligned closely with budget; Bakken saw a small overrun from child well challenges. Comps cost per foot improved 5% YoY to $1,200, with 30-day IP rates at 1,800 Boe/d per well, 12% above plan.

Facilities capex: budget $150 million versus actual $120 million—a 20% underrun. This includes midstream infrastructure like produced water recycling plants. In the Permian, spend reflected delays in a 10-mile flowline, saving cash while preserving optionality. Eagle Ford funded SWD wells recycling 70% of water volumes; Bakken was light. Overall, this underrun boosts flexibility, dropping facilities as a percentage of total D&C.

In aggregate, our $80 million net capex underrun YTD underscores leverage from our tech stack and supply chain hedging. Q4 guidance holds steady, positioning us for strong FCF.

Finally, on capital allocation priorities—dividends, share buybacks, and reinvestment. With Brent crude averaging $78 per barrel YTD and Henry Hub around $2.80/MMBtu, our operations generated $1.2 billion in free cash flow this quarter, bringing us to $4.1 billion for the first nine months—on track for $5.5 to $6 billion full-year.

Our philosophy is discipline first, returns second, growth third. We target returning 60-70% of FCF to shareholders, reinvesting the balance into opportunities with IRRs north of 20%. We've maintained this since 2021, driving 25% total shareholder return, outpacing the XLE.

First, dividends—our base quarterly dividend increased 8% to $0.65 per share, our 17th consecutive hike, yielding 4.2% forward—above peers. Payout ratio at 38% of adjusted earnings, with growth in the 7-10% range funded from operations, backed by 650,000 BOE/d production and midstream cash flows.

Second, share buybacks—we've executed $2.3 billion under our $4 billion authorization, repurchasing 4.2% of shares at $112 average—accreting $1.85 to EPS. $1.7 billion remains; we'll deploy when below our EV/BOE metric. Q4 expects $500-700 million.

Finally, reinvestment—$4.8 billion capex: 55% upstream, 25% midstream/downstream, 20% new energies. Upstream doubles down on Permian with 2.5-mile laterals; Guyana Yellowtail hits first oil next year. Internationally, Norway and Qatar add low-breakeven volumes. ESG includes $800 million in CCUS and digital tools boosting efficiency.

This framework de-levered us to 0.9x net debt/EBITDA. Questions welcome.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Chen for an operational update.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, John. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 412,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought the Pecos 12H well online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

Thank you, John. Good morning, everyone. I'll now turn to our refining segment, which delivered another quarter of strong results amid a volatile macro environment. Our refining portfolio consists of 10 world-class facilities with a total atmospheric distillation capacity of 2.1 million barrels per day, strategically located across the U.S. Gulf Coast, Midwest, and West Coast. Our assets benefit from a high Nelson Complexity Index average of 11.2, enabling superior clean product yields and flexibility to process a wide slate of crudes, from light WTI and Eagle Ford condensates to heavier Canadian heavy sour and Latin American imports.

Starting with throughput, we averaged 1.82 million barrels per day in Q3, representing a 7% increase year-over-year and a sequential uptick of 3% from Q2. This translated to an industry-leading utilization rate of 94%, well above the U.S. Gulf Coast peer average of 88% per EIA data. Gulf Coast throughput hit a record 1.1 million bpd, driven by robust light tight oil availability from the Permian Basin—where we sourced 45% of our feedstock at a favorable WTI basis—and optimized runs at our Port Arthur and Beaumont complexes. In the Midwest, our Lima and Canton refineries operated at 98% utilization, capitalizing on regional Canadian crude discounts amid pipeline constraints on Enbridge's Line 5. West Coast performance was solid at 92% utilization, though tempered by California-specific railcar loadings for CARB-compliant fuels. Notably, we navigated a planned 21-day turnaround at our Benicia refinery without major disruptions, minimizing offline days to just 2% of total capacity.

Turning to margins, our realized refining margin came in at $14.20 per barrel, a 15% improvement over Q3 last year and flat sequentially, despite headwinds from a narrowing 3-2-1 crack spread. The benchmark crack averaged $16.50/bbl in the Gulf Coast, down from $18.20 in Q2 due to softer distillate demand amid mild weather and elevated product inventories. However, we outperformed the benchmark by $2.30/bbl through superior product slate optimization—our gasoline yield of 48% and diesel/ULSD yield of 27% allowed us to capture premium pricing in Midwest diesel cracks, which traded at a $8/bbl uplift to NYMEX heating oil. Feedstock costs were well-controlled at $68/bbl net, benefiting from 20% sour crude processing at our high-complexity cokers and hydrocrackers, where we locked in Latin American Maya at a $4/bbl discount to Brent. Regionally, Gulf Coast margins held firm at $15.80/bbl, supported by export volumes of 450,000 bpd of jet fuel and gasoline to Europe and Latin America, where Singapore GRMs remained resilient above $8/bbl. Midwest margins were exceptional at $16.50/bbl, while West Coast came in at $11.20/bbl, pressured by elevated RIN costs—up 10% QoQ to $1.50/RIN for D4 biomass-based diesel compliance—and competition from imported CARB diesel.

On operational efficiency, we continue to drive best-in-class metrics, with cash operating costs per barrel declining 8% YoY to $5.10/bbl, reflecting disciplined expense management and yield improvements. Our variable costs were bolstered by a 2% reduction in natural gas consumption through cogeneration enhancements at five sites, saving $25 million annually. Distillate yields rose to 52% of total output, up from 49% last year, thanks to debottlenecking our hydrotreating capacity by 15,000 bpd across the portfolio—particularly the new 10,000 bpd hydrotreater at Port Arthur, which ensures IMO 2020-compliant VLSFO production at 95% conversion rates. Maintenance efficiency was outstanding, with turnaround costs 12% under budget at $450 million, and we completed FCC regenerator upgrades at Beaumont ahead of schedule, boosting propylene yields by 3% for alpha olefins sales into the petrochemical market. Energy intensity improved to 85,000 BTU per barrel, positioning us in the top quartile of Solomon Associates benchmarks. Environmentally, our renewable diesel production ramped to 25,000 bpd at our Rodeo facility, generating $50 million in RIN-waived margins and advancing our pathway to 100,000 bpd by 2026 via co-processing vegetable oils in existing hydrocrackers.

Strategically, these results underscore our focus on high-gradesheet, low-cost refining amid energy transition pressures. We've optimized our slate for 60% clean products, hedging 70% of Q4 cracks at $15/bbl floors, and are advancing $1.2 billion in growth capex, including a new alkylation unit at Lima for octane enhancement and isomerization expansions to meet rising EV-offset demand for premium fuels. Looking ahead, we see Q4 throughput of 1.85-1.95 million bpd, with margins supported by winter diesel demand and Permian supply growth, though monitoring geopolitical risks in the Middle East that could widen Brent-WTI spreads. We're well-positioned to capture upside from jet fuel rebound—up 12% YoY globally per IATA—as air travel normalizes.

Now I will turn it over to David Patel for an update on our exploration activities.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Basin and are planning to drill 10 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Brian Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Brian Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the refining segment performance, particularly throughput and margins?

Mike Reynolds: Good morning, Brian. Happy to elaborate. As Lisa detailed, our throughput hit 1.82 million bpd at 94% utilization, outpacing peers, with Gulf Coast records and strong regional plays. Margins at $14.20/bbl beat the benchmark through clean product optimization and sour crude discounts. Efficiency gains kept costs low at $5.10/bbl, and we're ramping renewables—positioned well for Q4 upside.

Operator: Our next question comes from Elena Vasquez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Elena Vasquez: Good morning. What are your expectations for production guidance next quarter and full year, including key factors?

John Harlan: Good morning, Elena. Q4 at 425-450k BOE/d, up sequentially, with 2025 at 460-485k—a 15% midpoint growth. Permian drives it with strong IPs and tech like AI seismic; Eagle Ford and DJ add balance. Hedged for $70-80 WTI, risks like OPEC+ factored in. Returns-focused, with 7 years Tier 1 inventory.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly: Could you please provide more color on proved reserves additions and capex breakdown?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Tom. On reserves, YTD additions of 285 MMBOE yield 188% RRR, 165% organic—Permian extensions shine with ApexStim fracs. Capex under by 7% net: drilling 4% under on efficiencies, comps slight over but IPs beat; facilities 20% under. Sets up FCF strength.

Operator: Our next question comes from Priya Singh with Citi. Please go ahead.

Priya Singh: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

David Patel: Good morning, Priya. Our Permian seismic unlocked high-potential spots, with 10 wells planned to mirror recent extensions adding MMBOE. Integrates with production ramp, bolstering 7+ year inventory and organic RRR >150%. Enhances strategy for returns-led growth, low breakevens.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Mike Reynolds for closing remarks.

Mike Reynolds: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
